basis: Benign tumour of the hypopharynx; pharynx belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Inflammation of dental pulp, usually driven by bacterial infection; classified here as a bacterial infectious disease.
Benign peripheral nerve sheath tumour arising from nerves in the gallbladder; definition takes precedence over malignant ancestors.
Clear cell sarcoma arising in tendons and aponeuroses; melanocytic differentiation does not establish a skin origin.
Inherited coagulation factor deficiency. Mucosal bleeding does not establish organ damage; joint and intracranial haemorrhage occur in 5-29%.
Polyp arising from vaginal tissue; reproductive organs have no axis.
Skeletal myopathy with diaphragmatic weakness (4/4); ventilatory failure does not establish intrinsic lung damage. Cardiomyopathy 1/4; brain imaging limited to 1 patient.
Inherited cardiomyopathy affecting cardiac muscle, with variable ventricular morphology and arrhythmias.
VZV infection of the ophthalmic trigeminal division and its cutaneous territory; keratitis, uveitis or other ocular disease develops in roughly 50%.
Disease of the pupil and iris.
Adenocarcinoma arising in the periampullary region of the duodenum; biliary obstruction alone does not establish hepatic involvement.
Primary skeletal muscle disorder. Motor delay reflects weakness; occasional respiratory involvement does not establish common intrinsic lung injury.
Craniosynostosis and cataracts are the defining skeletal and ocular abnormalities.
Obesity, intellectual disability and ocular defects define syndrome; femoral bowing/abnormal ossification occur in 30-79%. Dental abnormalities, also 30-79%, omitted by cap.
Tumour originates in the extrahepatic bile ducts; rhabdomyoblastic histology does not establish skeletal muscle involvement.
Dermatobia larvae infest skin and subcutaneous tissue, producing furuncular lesions.
Nonsyndromic inherited sideroblastic anaemia. Increased ferritin alone does not establish damaging iron deposition in another organ.
Developmental dental disease with abnormal dentin, enamel, tooth number and roots; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Acute nicotine poisoning causes autonomic nervous system dysfunction; nausea and vomiting do not establish gastrointestinal tissue injury.
Metabolic bone disorder defined by loss of bone mass and microarchitecture, with skeletal fragility.
Ptosis, high myopia and lens dislocation define the syndrome; structural fingernail dysplasia is reported in 30-79%.
Carcinoma arising in the vulva, a reproductive organ outside the axes. HPV is a risk factor and does not make the carcinoma an infectious disease.
Squamous cell carcinoma of the hypopharynx; pharynx belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; pulmonary hyaline membranes indicate lung injury reported in 2/3 patients, though the evidence is a very small series.
Space-associated vestibular adaptation disorder; nausea, vomiting and dizziness do not establish damage to additional organs.
